A 4x4 jungle safari is the easiest way to see Koh Samui's interior in one day: Na Muang Waterfall, the Secret Buddha Garden up a road most scooters can't manage, Wat Khunaram's mummified monk, Hin Ta and Hin Yai, a hilltop viewpoint and lunch. Shared safaris run 7–8.5 hours, roughly 08:30–16:30, and cost 1,500–2,100 THB per adult in 2026 with lunch and transfer from the main beach areas (children from 800 THB). Private 4x4s for your own group start at about 7,500 THB. None of the safaris we sell includes elephant riding.

A typical route, stop by stop

Every operator shuffles the order to avoid crowds, but a classic day looks like this:

  1. 08:30 Pickup from your hotel in the main beach areas.
  2. 09:15 Hin Ta and Hin Yai, the Grandfather and Grandmother rocks at the south end of Lamai.
  3. 10:00 Wat Khunaram and the mummified monk Luang Pho Daeng.
  4. 10:45 Na Muang Waterfall 1: swim in the pool below the 18 m fall.
  5. 11:45 The 4x4 part: steep concrete and dirt tracks up to the central ridge.
  6. 12:45 Lunch at a hilltop restaurant with sea views.
  7. 13:45 Secret Buddha Garden (Tarnim Magic Garden).
  8. 15:00 Big Buddha on the way back north.
  9. 16:30 Back at your hotel.

Shared or private safari

Shared safaris are good value and sociable, but you move at the group's pace and spend the first hour collecting other guests. A private 4x4 lets you start early, skip what you don't care about and stay longer at the waterfall.

  • Private island tour by 4x4: 8 hours with driver for up to 10 people, 9,500 THB per vehicle; an English-speaking guide costs 2,500 THB extra and a set lunch 250 THB per person. See the private tour.
  • Private version of the discovery safari: from 7,500 THB with driver only, or 10,500 THB with guide and lunch for up to 5, on request.
  • Private small-group off-road safari: any day from 8,500 THB for 1–2 guests, on request.

International booking sites list private safaris at around US$279 per person, so for two or more people a private 4x4 booked locally is usually much cheaper.

What to wear and bring

  • Swimwear under your clothes for the waterfall, plus a towel.
  • A sarong or light shirt and trousers to cover shoulders and knees at the temples.
  • Shoes with grip you can wear in water; the rocks at Na Muang are slippery.
  • Sunglasses and a cap with a strap: the open trucks are windy.
  • Cash in small notes for entry fees, donations, drinks and tips.
  • Insect repellent and sunscreen.

Good to know before you go

  • It's bumpy. The open-backed trucks bounce on the steep tracks. Not advised during pregnancy, with back or spine problems or for children under 4.
  • Child seats. Open safari trucks have bench seats, not child seats. With a toddler, take a private minibus tour instead.
  • Rainy season. From October to December the tracks are muddy and the waterfalls are at their best. Tours still run; operators may skip the steepest track after heavy rain.
  • Heat. It's 30–33 °C in the middle of the day from April to September. Drink at every stop.
  • Shopping stops. Some itineraries include a coconut or rubber demonstration with a shop. You don't have to buy anything.

Do it yourself by scooter or car

Most of the stops are on or near the ring road and easy to reach yourself: Big Buddha, Wat Plai Laem, Hin Ta and Hin Yai, Wat Khunaram and Na Muang 1 all have car parks. The Secret Buddha Garden is the exception: its access road is very steep and narrow with a rough last stretch, so go by 4x4 or on a tour, not on a rental scooter. If you ride, Thai law requires a helmet, and you need a licence that covers motorbikes plus an International Driving Permit to be legal and insured. Read our scooter rental guide, car rental guide and getting around Koh Samui first. For the walks on the way, see Koh Samui waterfalls and hiking and viewpoints.

Animal welfare on safari tours

We don't sell elephant riding, animal shows or photo stops with chained animals. Five of the shared safaris we sell include no animal activities at all. Two include an elephant-feeding stop with no riding or bathing; the feeding is short and part of a long day, not a sanctuary visit. If elephants are the reason you're going, book a dedicated visit instead: our elephant sanctuary guide explains how to tell an ethical venue from a camp.

Prices in 2026

The shared safari market price on Samui is about 1,700 THB per adult in 2026 for 7 hours with lunch, entry fees and transfer. Our shared safaris cost 1,500–2,100 THB per adult, and child prices run from 800 THB (ex-army jeep, ages 5–12) to 1,800 THB (vegan-lunch safari, ages 4–11). Read each product's inclusions: entry fees are included on the kayak, vegan-lunch and elephant-feeding safaris, while on the ex-army jeep safari you pay about 100 THB for the Secret Buddha Garden yourself.
